narrative.overview:
The Workbench is where the notebook's experiments are set up and run. It is a working tool, not a page to read: one guided step at a time, every instrument labelled, every run's cost shown before it starts, and the command each step writes kept at the foot of the screen. It shares the site's and the catalog's foundation (the same tokens, Highlighter Lime, the heavy grotesk, monospace for everything exact) at an app's scale: titles are 30px, text is 15px, corners are small, and the screen is organised around a journey rail on the left and a help panel that opens on the right.

The voice stays confident and plain, and it explains. Each field has a one-line hint under it and a "?" that opens more; the rare settings and the command are folded away; hints can be turned off. Lime marks what is done or current and the one action a screen asks for; three status colours say how a check came out.

- A journey rail: each step a dot, filled lime when done, a lime ring when current. - Lettered parts on a screen, each a hairline block with its own title, "?" and status. - Forms on a label column (180px) beside the field, with a hint under each. - Status colours (ok, warn, bad) kept apart from the accent and from the catalog's data colours. - The command a screen runs, folded at its foot; every view also an `evh` command.

rules.name: The Done Is Lime Rule
rules.body: Lime says a step is done or current, or names the one action to take; a check's result is always a status colour.

rules.name: The Status Is Not Data Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red say how a check came out, never what kind of model an arm is (the catalog's colours do that).

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Selection is a lime ring and hover is a darker border; nothing rises.

dos: **Do** give each screen one primary action, in lime.
**Do** put a one-line hint under each field and the rest behind its "?".
**Do** show a run's cost before it starts and the command each step writes.
**Do** keep status colours for a check's result and lime for done, current and the next action.
donts: **Don't** use a status colour for a model's kind, or lime for a check's result.
**Don't** lift a selected card or block with a shadow; use the lime ring.
**Don't** put every key of a file in a form: ask only what a person decides at that step.
**Don't** show a value the harness did not compute; a mockup's pretended value is labelled.
